en: There comes a time, O Āgñāta-kauṇḍinya, when this world dissolves. When the world is dissolving, for the most part, sentient beings are reborn in the Ābhāsvara host of gods. There they exist as beings possessing form, mind-made, complete, with all faculties unimpaired.

Endowed with all major and minor limbs, beautiful, abiding in their own radiance, self-luminous, traveling through the air, feeding on joy, nourished by joy, long-lived, they remain for a long duration.
At that time, indeed, the great earth becomes a single body of water, a single ocean. Upon that great earth, which has become a single body of water—

In that single-ocean world, the sap, condensed by the wind, spreads out; just as the sap of boiled milk, when condensed, spreads out, even so in that great earth which has become a single ocean of water, the sap, condensed by the wind, spreads out. That becomes the essence of the earth, endowed with color and endowed with fragrance.
It is endowed with flavor; its color is like fresh butter, and its taste is like pure, unadulterated honey.

There comes a time when this world evolves. As the world evolves, beings—due to the exhaustion of their lifespan, the exhaustion of their karma, and the exhaustion of their merit—pass away from the Ābhāsvara divine realm and descend to attain a human state here on earth. They...
Furthermore, those possessing form remain for a long duration as previously described.

At that time, indeed, neither the sun nor the moon was discerned; neither night nor day, month nor half-month, season nor moment (kṣaṇa), instant (lava), nor hour (muhūrta) was discerned... there was neither female nor male; a being was designated by the single number "being."

Then, a certain being of a greedy disposition tasted the essence of the earth with the tip of his finger. As he tasted it more and more, he craved it more and more; as he craved it more and more, he began to consume it by taking mouthfuls. Other beings saw that being consuming the essence of the earth by taking mouthfuls.

And having seen this, those beings also tasted the essence of the earth with their fingertips. Just as they tasted it, as described previously, until they began to consume it in mouthfuls. And because those beings consumed that essence of the earth by way of mouthfuls, firmness and heaviness became manifest in their bodies, and a beautiful complexion appeared.

[The light] disappeared; darkness appeared in the world. Now, Vasiṣṭha, it is the natural order of things that because of the appearance of darkness in the world, the sun and moon become known, and so forth, as in section 4.
